name: Question 4
problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(\sqrt{5},-1,2)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k.$
worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=\sqrt{5}i-j+2k,$ and $n=\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) & =(\sqrt{5}i-j+2k)\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) \\ r\cdot (\sqrt{5}i-3j+2k) & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point P(5,−1,2) and is perpendicular to the vector n=5i−3j+2k.

a
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=6
b
 r⋅(5i−j−2k)=12
c
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=1
d
 r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=12
e
 r⋅(5i+2j−3k)=6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=5i−j+2k, and n=5i−3j+2k is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point P(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−p)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and p is the position vector of P.

So, we have (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n−p⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅(5i−3j+2k)=(5i−j+2k)⋅(5i−3j+2k)r⋅(5i−3j+2k)=12.
